questions.q: Why isn't a successful COPY return code sufficient proof that a load is correct?
options: A load can return successfully while still silently skipping a partition, duplicating files, or dropping rows
Redshift always reports load errors as warnings, never as success
COPY never actually returns a success status
Because Athena and Redshift use different row counts by design
questions.explain: None of those failure modes produce an error message — the load just quietly returns the wrong result.

questions.q: What does the curated-side validation query in this lesson actually read from?
options: The Redshift system catalog tables
A snapshot of analytics.fact_orders taken before the load
The Parquet files in the curated S3 zone, through the Glue Catalog table the ETL job's sink registered
The raw S3 zone's uncleaned CSV files
questions.explain: The curated-side query runs against northfield_catalog.northfield_orders_curated, independent of Redshift entirely.

questions.q: What two numbers does the standard validation check compare between the curated zone and fact_orders?
options: Query runtime and compute cost
File size and partition count
Row count and a numeric sum (order_total)
Table name and schema name
questions.explain: The check compares row counts and a SUM(order_total) on both sides.

questions.q: Why isn't a row-count match alone quite enough to confirm a correct load?
options: COUNT(*) is not supported in Athena
Row counts are never reliable in Redshift
It's possible for the right number of rows to land with wrong values in them, which a count alone wouldn't catch
Row counts can't be computed without a full table scan
questions.explain: A sum check catches value-level mismatches that a matching row count by itself would miss.

questions.q: Why does this lesson's validation check get reused later in the chapter rather than being a one-time step?
options: Because the query itself changes every time it's run
Because after a real bug fix in Lesson 13, the same check is what actually confirms the fix worked
Because the curated zone's schema changes daily
Because Redshift requires it to be re-run every hour automatically
questions.explain: "The fix compiled" is as weak a signal as "COPY didn't error" — the same count-and-sum check is what actually confirms correctness.
